title: The Threads
subtitle: How the whole project connects
manifesto: A thread is not a tag. A tag tells you what something is about. A thread tells you why it keeps coming back. Every clip, chapter, room, note, song, object, pass, and memory can carry more than one wire. The project only starts making sense when those wires cross. This is the board behind the whole house.
short_explainer: Threads are the book's nervous system. They are how one clip becomes part of a chapter, how one room becomes part of the archive, how one pass carries more than a serial number, and how the audience learns where they entered the story.

research_frame.thread_theory: Threads are the project's artistic and intellectual model for recurring patterns: events, objects, memories, systems, and reactions that return, cross, stabilize, and reshape meaning over time.
research_frame.crack_capitalism: The system mirror is structural: reward loops, status pressure, scarcity, platform pressure, and the culture of never enough. The claim is about social logic and documented experience, not fake certainty.
research_frame.media_strategy: Website as map, Discord as live room, YouTube as public documentary spine, Patreon as back room, Trap Passes as access identity, and the book/soundtrack as permanent objects.

theory_cards.title: Evidence
theory_cards.summary: A clip, object, room, or caption can belong to more than one thread at once. Nothing in this project lives alone.

theory_cards.title: Return
theory_cards.summary: A thread gains weight when the same pattern keeps coming back in a new form. The repetition is the clue.

theory_cards.title: Crossing
theory_cards.summary: The strongest story moments happen where two wires hit each other: grief and money, addiction and writing, platform war and public witness.

theory_cards.title: Limits
theory_cards.summary: The map is an artistic and intellectual framework. It shows how lived experience repeats, mutates, and builds meaning over time.

origin.title: January 22 / The Origin / Blast Crater
origin.summary: January 22 is the fracture point. Everything routes back through this day: grief, collapse, money panic, addiction logic, public witness, and the decision to build instead of disappear. This is not just a date. It is the first knot in the map.

book.title: The Book
book.headline: Real stories. The book.
book.summary: IM HIGH ON CRACK AND I HAVE A GUN is not a repetitive recovery slogan, not a cautionary poster, and not another polished addiction memoir cleaned up enough to make everyone comfortable.
book.body: It is a documentary-book experience carved from inside the wreckage: part memoir, part field report, part confession, part indictment, and part archive object. The clips, notes, rooms, grief, money panic, systems, broken bodies, and broken timelines get dragged into the light without being softened into something fake.
book.footer: This is not fiction. This is not glamorous. This is the evidence. This is the diagnosis. This is what happens when a breaking point becomes a thread.

author.name: Ryan Homanics
author.title: Author / Documentarian
author.summary: Ryan Homanics is a Pittsburgh writer, documentarian, and author of Dopesick: The American Addiction to Heroin and Profit.
author.body: His work moves between memoir, social indictment, field report, and underground archive, dragging addiction, class, grief, psychosis, survival, and systemic collapse into plain view.
author.footer: With a voice that is educated, damaged, furious, and strangely devotional, Homanics writes from inside the wreckage, turning personal ruin into evidence, diagnosis, and thread.

threads.title: Addiction Machine
threads.summary: The engine: ritual, survival, time, compulsion, repetition, and the way the machine keeps asking for another loop.

threads.title: Psychosis Loop
threads.summary: No sleep. Pattern hunting. Rooftop logic. Reality bending. The dangerous feeling that every coincidence has teeth.

threads.title: Grief / Loss
threads.summary: The locked room underneath everything. The room does not open cleanly. It bleeds into the rest of the map.

threads.title: Cats / Home / Tenderness
threads.summary: Proof that love survived inside the wreckage. The only clean place, the interruption, the home signal.

threads.title: Writing Inside The Fire
threads.summary: Book, documentary, songs, notes, evidence, and the act of turning collapse into a permanent object.

threads.title: Money Desperation
threads.summary: Survival math. Gas money. Rent logic. Next 24 hours. The pressure that makes the machine louder.

threads.title: System Mirror
threads.summary: Crack capitalism as a public mirror. More-more-more. Addiction as private spiral and social logic at the same time.

threads.title: Platform War
threads.summary: Bans, rebuilds, algorithm pressure, migration, Discord as home base, and the move from channel to world.

threads.title: Trap Pass Lore
threads.summary: Keys to hidden rooms, drops, participation, proof, holder status, and the moment the audience starts carrying the map.

threads.title: Self-Destruction vs Creation
threads.summary: Burn it down versus build something permanent. The fork in the road that decides whether the archive becomes ash or architecture.

threads.title: Public Project / Witness
threads.summary: Audience enters, reacts, shares, joins, votes, and watches the building happen. The witness becomes part of the evidence trail.

threads.title: Ending Convergence
threads.summary: All threads collide and come back together. The map stops being separate rooms and becomes one house.

crossings.title: Addiction Machine x Money Desperation
crossings.lead: This is the survival math loop.
crossings.body: The machine needs time, money, fuel, movement, panic, and one more bad calculation. Money desperation does not sit beside addiction. It feeds the engine.

crossings.title: Psychosis Loop x Platform War
crossings.lead: Private reality bends. Public systems react.
crossings.body: The same mind that starts seeing signs everywhere eventually meets algorithms, bans, reporting systems, platform pressure, and forced migration. The loop leaves the room and becomes a distribution problem.

crossings.title: Cats / Home / Tenderness x Ending Convergence
crossings.lead: The softest thread becomes one of the strongest.
crossings.body: The cats, the room, the home signal, and the moments of tenderness prove the project is not only destruction. They are what survives long enough to pull the map back together.
crossings.feeds: Home, witness, final chapter, public memory

flow: Addiction feeds money desperation and psychosis loops.
Cats and home push back against collapse.
The system mirror turns private pain into social critique.
Trap Passes make the audience participants.
In the end, all threads converge.
